diagnosis:
Failed checkpoint theta-gate inside the flake gate ladder, before test/final-bar ever ran: the fleet gate build of `checks.x86_64-linux.spec-lint` exits 1 on exactly one blocking defect, `specs/eta/spec.md:4: L2: Governs names `silent-factory-worklists/eta.json`, which does not exist at this revision`, followed by `spec-lint: specs/eta carries a blocking defect`. Evidence and scope: the transcript at commit 8fc4597657a18d88dcb1a85298fd521366f9dc8b shows the multi-host VM test suite finishing green and only the `spec-lint` attribute failing; the other lines in the tail are the must-fail fixture corpus printing its expected defects, not new failures. The regression is a cross-task interaction inside theta, not a defect in theta-gate itself: `charter-retirement` (630479f0) retired the ETA charter and `residue-sweep` (94a4d476) deleted `silent-factory-worklists/eta.json` along with the other closed worklists, both squarely inside their declared conflictDomains (`residue-sweep` owns `silent-factory-worklists`), while `specs/eta/spec.md` still carries `Status: ratified 2026-08-17` and `Governs: silent-factory-worklists/eta.json`. Per `specs/README.md` section 3 and `crates/spec-lint/src/lint.rs:304`, the L2 existence check on `Governs` fires only when the status block parses as ratified, so retiring the governed worklist without moving the spec out of the ratified state is what turned the standing consumer red. theta-gate is a checkpoint with an empty diff and a worklist-fixed argv, so it has no authorized paths of its own and cannot retry into a fix. No theta task can repair it either: the only `specs/**` grant anywhere in `silent-factory-worklists/theta.json` is `specs/README.md` on `charter-retirement`, and `specs/eta/spec.md` is written by nobody in this campaign; `residue-sweep`'s own goal additionally forbids touching `specs/eta/evidence/**` as frozen evidence. The repair is a one-line status transition that the house format already provides for exactly this lifecycle end: flip the Status line to `closed <release-ref>`, which clears L2 without resurrecting the deleted worklist, without editing the frozen evidence tree, and without weakening the lint. Restoring `silent-factory-worklists/eta.json` is the wrong direction, since it would undo the sweep the campaign was armed to perform. This needs new write authority over `specs/eta/spec.md`, so the verdict is blocked with an amendment-task proposal; note also that `test/final-bar/run` has never executed at this revision because the `&&` short-circuited, so the amendment lane must leave theta-gate to re-run the full ladder afterward.

proposal.goal: Close the eta spec so the retired worklist stops being a dangling ratified pointer, restoring checks.x86_64-linux.spec-lint to green. The eta campaign ended at 321e29111dc4688c5609ce5c3b4ddc6d0be84182 (the same pinned commit README.md and specs/README.md already use as the archival copy for the retired charters and zeta-learnings), and residue-sweep has since deleted silent-factory-worklists/eta.json. Do: (1) In specs/eta/spec.md line 3, replace `Status: ratified 2026-08-17` with `Status: closed 321e29111dc4688c5609ce5c3b4ddc6d0be84182`. specs/README.md section 3 declares the closed form (`Status: proposed | ratified YYYY-MM-DD | closed <release-ref>`) and section 6 makes closure the campaign's terminal lifecycle state; crates/spec-lint/src/lint.rs applies the L2 Governs-must-exist check only while the status parses as ratified, so this single line clears the defect. (2) Leave line 4 `Governs: silent-factory-worklists/eta.json` byte-identical — a closed spec keeps naming the worklist it governed, and the worklist bytes live at the pinned commit. (3) Add one CHANGELOG.md entry under the top heading recording that specs/eta moved to closed and naming the release-ref. Boundaries: change exactly one line in specs/eta/spec.md and add one CHANGELOG.md entry. Do not restore silent-factory-worklists/eta.json or any other deleted worklist. Do not touch specs/eta/evidence/** — it is frozen evidence. Do not touch specs/eta/trace.json, specs/README.md, specs/zeta/**, crates/spec-lint/**, or any file not named above; specs/zeta/spec.md is `Status: proposed` and is correctly silent under L2, so it needs no change.

diagnosis: Blocked on authority, not on the change: the ownership gate conflict-domains failed because specs/eta/spec.md is an authority-surface path in the protected set (governing-spec-directory: the governing spec of identity "eta"), and a declared conflictDomain does not grant a protected path. The committed work on the lane branch (eb63a4f0) is otherwise exactly what the task specifies: specs/eta/spec.md line 3 now reads 'Status: closed 321e29111dc4688c5609ce5c3b4ddc6d0be84182', line 4 'Governs: silent-factory-worklists/eta.json' is byte-identical, silent-factory-worklists holds only theta.json, specs/eta/evidence/ is untouched, and CHANGELOG.md gains one entry naming specs/eta and the release-ref. Only two paths were touched and both sit inside the declared conflictDomains, so no boundary was crossed and no smaller edit exists that clears spec-lint L2 — the L2 Governs-must-exist check fires precisely on the status line the driver protects. No retry can succeed: any attempt that satisfies eta-spec-status-closed must write specs/eta/spec.md, which re-trips conflict-domains at the ownership stage before acceptance criteria ever run. The secondary result-projection-timeout on the spec-build-driver finalMessage capture is a consequence of the same non-zero ownership exit, not an independent machinery fault, so this is not transient. The operator or coordinator must land the specs/eta/spec.md byte change by hand (or grant the governing-spec-directory authority surface for this task), after which the CHANGELOG.md half and the spec-lint oracle need no further work.
